Microbiology Spectrum.title: Integrative multi-database analysis of a microbiome-based survival model in gastric cancer.
Microbiology Spectrum.abstract: This study evaluated a gastric cancer survival model based on tumor-associated microbial DNA profiles and examined their relationships with bulk host marker-expression scores. Microbiome, host-transcriptome, and clinical data from 118 matched TCMA/TCGA-STAD specimens (109 primary tumors and nine adjacent tissues) were integrated. After random 7:3 split and exclusion of incomplete samples, 68 training cases and 32 validation cases remained. A multi-step screening identified survival-associated microbial features, followed by PCA to construct a microbial risk score (MRS). An integrated model combining MRS, age, and sex was built, with reviewer-requested tumor-only sensitivity analyses for pathologic stage and Helicobacter. Neisseria and Veillonella showed hazard ratio estimates below 1 across multiple transformations, with Actinomyces showing the same direction at a trend-level significance threshold. Within the original age-sex model, MRS was associated with overall survival (HR = 1.73, P = 0.002). The integrated model (C-index 0.707) outperformed the age-sex comparator (0.590) and the microbiological-only model (0.672) in the training set. In the training set, high-risk patients had shorter median survival (457 vs 2,100 days, P = 0.001; 1-/2-/3-year AUCs: 0.683, 0.760, 0.768). In the held-out internal validation subset, the model yielded a C-index of 0.636 (P = 0.0494). In 109 primary-tumor specimens, genus-level Helicobacter DNA signal correlated with bulk B-cell and mast-cell marker-expression scores after multiple-testing correction (rho = 0.247, q = 0.049; rho = 0.282, q = 0.030); the dendritic-cell association was not retained (q = 0.271), and Helicobacter did not improve a tumor-only three-genus survival model (likelihood-ratio P = 0.803). The age-sex-microbiome model showed exploratory survival discrimination; a post hoc tumor-only analysis did not demonstrate incremental value of the three genera beyond age, sex, and pathologic stage (likelihood-ratio P = 0.571). The Helicobacter associations with bulk B-cell and mast-cell marker-expression scores require orthogonal validation.IMPORTANCEThis study examines microbiome-informed survival stratification in gastric cancer. Using tumor-associated microbial DNA profiles from 118 matched specimens, the researchers built a survival model combining three genus-level features (Actinomyces, Neisseria, and Veillonella) with age and sex. In the training set, this model outperformed the age-sex comparator and distinguished high-risk patients (median survival 457 days) from low-risk patients (2,100 days). In the held-out internal validation subset, the model yielded a C-index of 0.636. Additionally, genus-level Helicobacter DNA signal correlated with bulk B-cell and mast-cell marker-expression scores in the tumor-only analysis. These results define an exploratory microbiome-based framework for further prognostic and biological validation in gastric cancer.

Microbiology Spectrum.title: High prevalence of CTX-M-associated multidrug resistance and diagnostic accuracy of NG-Test CTX-M Multi among ESBL-producing Escherichia coli in Vietnam.
Microbiology Spectrum.abstract: CTX-M enzymes are the predominant extended-spectrum β-lactamases (ESBLs) worldwide, yet local epidemiology in Vietnam remains incompletely characterized. This study investigated CTX-M prevalence among ESBL-producing Escherichia coli from inpatients at a tertiary-care hospital in Ho Chi Minh City and evaluated the diagnostic performance of the NG-Test CTX-M Multi assay. A prospective cross-sectional study was conducted at FV Hospital from January 2024 to April 2025. ESBL-producing E. coli flagged by the VITEK 2 Advanced Expert System (AES) were tested with NG-Test CTX-M Multi (NG Biotech, France). Antimicrobial susceptibility testing followed CLSI M100 guidelines (2024). Diagnostic accuracy was assessed against multiplex real-time PCR (Allplex Entero-DR Assay) in a blinded evaluation of 76 isolates. Of the 461 E. coli isolates, 180 (39.0%) were ESBL producers; CTX-M was detected in 124 (68.9%). CTX-M-positive isolates showed significantly higher resistance to cefotaxime (98.4% vs 28.5%), cefepime (78.2% vs 10.7%), gentamicin (37.9% vs 12.7%), and ciprofloxacin (74.8% vs 73.2%); all P < 0.05. Carbapenems and amikacin retained high susceptibility (>95%) in both groups. CTX-M-positive isolates exhibited broader resistance profiles (≥6 antimicrobial classes: 68.9% vs 27.8%). AmpC flagging was more frequent in CTX-M-negative isolates (69.6% vs 28.2%; P < 0.001). NG-Test CTX-M Multi demonstrated 92.1% sensitivity (95% confidence interval [CI], 79.2-97.3), 94.7% specificity (95% CI, 82.7-98.5), PPV 94.6%, and NPV 92.3%. CTX-M was the dominant ESBL mechanism and was associated with broader multidrug resistance. NG-Test CTX-M Multi showed high diagnostic accuracy, supporting its role as a rapid screening tool; however, larger validation studies are warranted.IMPORTANCEInfections caused by Escherichia coli producing extended-spectrum beta-lactamases (ESBLs) pose a significant challenge for clinical management because they limit the effectiveness of commonly used antibiotics. CTX-M enzymes are now well established as the dominant ESBL determinants worldwide; however, their local prevalence and associated antimicrobial resistance patterns continue to vary across healthcare settings. In this study, we investigated the prevalence of CTX-M-producing E. coli and their resistance profiles in a tertiary care hospital in Vietnam. Our findings demonstrate a substantial burden of CTX-M-associated multidrug resistance affecting both hospital- and community-associated infections. In addition, the evaluation of a rapid lateral flow immunoassay for CTX-M detection highlights its potential role as a practical screening tool to support timely antimicrobial decision-making and infection control efforts. Together, these results provide clinically relevant data to support antimicrobial stewardship and optimize the management of infections caused by resistant E. coli.

Microbiology Spectrum.title: Organic manure is associated with enhanced potential nitrogenase activity and Geobacter enrichment in flooded subtropical paddy soil.
Microbiology Spectrum.abstract: [UNLABELLED] The effect of the organic manure and synthetic fertilizer application ratio on biological nitrogen fixation (BNF) by iron-reducing bacteria (IRB) remains unclear. Hence, a microcosm flooding incubation experiment was conducted with four treatments with the same N input, including no N fertilization (CT), 100% urea N (U), 100% organic manure N (M), and a 1:1 combination of urea N and organic manure N (UM). Organic manure application significantly influenced the potential nitrogenase activity and Fe2+/Fe3+ ratio on day 35 (P < 0.01). Compared to the U treatments, the M treatment showed a 196.2% increase in potential nitrogenase activity and a 131.0% increase in Fe2+/Fe3+ ratio (P < 0.05). Relative to the CT and U treatment, the UM treatment significantly increased absolute abundance of IRB by 88.9% and 100.3%, and the relative abundance of IRB by 222.5% and 194.0%, respectively (P < 0.05). At the genus level, IRB communities were dominated by Geobacter (82.5-90.5%). Organic manure application significantly decreased co-occurrence network complexity while increasing modularity (P < 0.05). Soil C/N ratio was identified as the key factor driving potential nitrogenase activity (P < 0.01), and a network module dominated by Geobacter was the key taxa positively associated with potential nitrogenase activity (P < 0.05). Collectively, organic manure applied alone significantly enhanced BNF potential and iron reduction in flooded subtropical paddy soil, whereas combined application of organic manure N and synthetic fertilizer N at a ratio of 1:1 optimized IRB community assembly and network stability. [IMPORTANCE] Substituting synthetic fertilizers with organic manure enhances potential biological nitrogen fixation (BNF) in paddy soils. This study demonstrates that under equal N levels, organic manure applied alone significantly strengthens potential nitrogenase activity in flooded subtropical paddy soils; whereas combined application of organic manure N and synthetic fertilizer N at a 1:1 ratio optimizes microbial community structure assembly and network stability. More importantly, we reveal that organic manure substitution improves soil C/N ratios, thereby enhancing iron reduction and strengthening BNF potential. These findings provide insights into effective management strategies to promote natural N-supplementation through BNF in paddy soil.

Microbiology Spectrum.title: The essential NuA4 scaffold protein EafA supports histone H4 acetylation and filamentous growth in Aspergillus nidulans.
Microbiology Spectrum.abstract: [UNLABELLED] NuA4 is a conserved multisubunit histone acetyltransferase complex that regulates transcription and genome maintenance. Here, we characterized the function of EafA, the Aspergillus nidulans ortholog of the yeast NuA4 scaffold protein Eaf1. Heterokaryon rescue indicated that eafA is essential for viability under the conditions tested, while conditional repression severely restricted colony growth, and altered early conidial development and hyphal morphology. Repression of eafA also increased sensitivity to hydroxyurea and methyl methanesulfonate and was accompanied by reduced H4K5 and H4K12 acetylation. Simultaneous K5R/K12R substitutions in histone H4 caused a marked growth defect, providing genetic support for a functional link between EafA-associated H4 acetylation and fungal development. Together, these findings identify EafA as an essential nuclear Eaf1 ortholog that supports H4 acetylation, filamentous growth, and genotoxic-stress tolerance in A. nidulans. [IMPORTANCE] Filamentous fungi grow through continuous, polarized hyphal extension, a process that requires coordinated regulation of gene activity. However, how conserved histone-acetylating complexes support this distinctive growth pattern is not well understood. Here, we show that EafA, the Aspergillus nidulans counterpart of a protein that organizes such a complex in yeast, is required for viability under the conditions tested. Reduced EafA expression lowered histone H4 acetylation, altered early conidial development and hyphal morphology, and increased sensitivity to agents that damage genetic material. Substitution of the affected histone sites also strongly impaired fungal growth. These findings connect a conserved chromatin-regulatory system with filamentous development and genome protection and reveal an essential function for EafA in a filamentous fungus.

Microbiology Spectrum.title: Sustained reduction of blood culture contamination with a dedicated phlebotomy team.
Microbiology Spectrum.abstract: [UNLABELLED] Blood culture contamination and inadequate fill volumes compromise the diagnosis of bloodstream infections. While dedicated phlebotomy teams improve these metrics, evidence regarding long-term sustainability is scarce. We evaluated the impact of a 24/7 dedicated phlebotomy team on blood culture quality using a 9-year longitudinal data set. In this retrospective cohort study at a 1,300-bed tertiary hospital, we analyzed 505,752 adult blood culture sets collected between 2015 and 2023. Following the transition to a dedicated phlebotomy team in March 2017 in all clinical units except the emergency room (ER), we evaluated the intervention's effect using difference-in-differences (DID) analyses, with cultures collected by non-dedicated ER staff serving as a concurrent control. The dedicated team demonstrated a significantly lower contamination rate (0.22% [586/261,480]) than concurrent non-dedicated staff (0.80% [1,171/145,772]; P < 0.001), corresponding to a 56.6% reduction in the adjusted odds of contamination in the general wards (adjusted odds ratio = 0.43; P < 0.001). Mean fill volume per bottle was higher for the dedicated team (4.61 mL vs 2.16 mL; P < 0.001). Although the overall true positivity rate was lower for the dedicated team (6.24% vs 8.89%, P < 0.001), unit-stratified and DID analyses indicated a composition effect driven by higher baseline positivity in the ER, where non-dedicated staff predominantly operated. Within the same units, true positivity did not decrease after implementation. Trajectory analysis revealed that individual contamination rates stabilized after 13 months of continuous service. Sustained, negligible contamination rates and improved fill volumes are achievable through proficiency from dedicated training and long-term retention of specialized personnel. [IMPORTANCE] Contaminated blood cultures and poor sample volumes significantly compromise diagnostic accuracy, patient safety, and antimicrobial stewardship. While dedicated phlebotomy teams are widely recommended to mitigate these preanalytical errors, evidence regarding their long-term durability and the time required for personnel to achieve technical proficiency remains limited. In this 9-year study of over half a million blood cultures, we demonstrate that a dedicated team effectively minimizes contamination by skin bacteria and optimizes blood volumes for detecting bloodstream pathogens. Uniquely, our trajectory analysis reveals a 13-month learning curve required for personnel to achieve this high level of technical proficiency. These findings emphasize that maximizing diagnostic certainty requires hospitals to not only deploy specialized collection teams but also actively prioritize staff retention.

Microbiology Spectrum.title: Phage therapy reduces bacterial burden and inflammation in a neutropenic murine sepsis model caused by hyperinvasive carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae.
Microbiology Spectrum.abstract: [UNLABELLED] Klebsiella pneumoniae is an emerging opportunistic pathogen associated with severe clinical outcomes, and carbapenem-resistant K. pneumoniae (CRKP) has become a critical threat requiring alternative therapeutic strategies. Phage therapy has recently gained attention as a promising alternative to combat antimicrobial resistance. However, its efficacy alone and in combination with antibiotics in immunocompromised hosts remains understudied. Here, we established a cyclophosphamide-induced neutropenic murine sepsis model due to a hyperinvasive CRKP strain carrying multiple virulence factors. In vitro, ceftazidime-avibactam (CAZ-AVI) at 8/4 μg/mL was required to suppress growth of this strain for 48 h, and this concentration was slightly reduced to 4/4 μg/mL when combined with a cocktail of three taxonomically distinct phages (P24, P39, and P49). In vivo, a single dose of the phage cocktail (9 × 108 plaque-forming units/mouse), administered intravenously or intraperitoneally following bacterial challenge, achieved 2.5-5.1 log10 reductions of bacterial burdens across multiple tissues and organs. Correspondingly, serum tumor necrosis factor-α, interleukin-6, and interleukin-1β levels decreased significantly, and histopathological analysis revealed markedly mitigated inflammatory infiltration and tissue damage in the lung and liver. Both administration routes achieved comparable outcomes. Furthermore, in a delayed-treatment survival experiment, treatment with the phage cocktail combined with CAZ-AVI, initiated 2 h after lethal challenge, resulted in an 83.3% survival over the 28-day observation period. In contrast, all untreated mice succumbed within 2 days, and phage cocktail alone resulted in only 8.3% survival. Collectively, these findings provide in vivo evidence supporting the combination of phage cocktail and CAZ-AVI against CRKP infection in immunocompromised hosts. [IMPORTANCE] Carbapenem-resistant K. pneumoniae (CRKP) has emerged as a critical threat to global public health, causing life-threatening infections, disproportionately affecting immunocompromised patients who often fail to respond to conventional antibiotic therapy and experience high mortality rates. However, the efficacy of phage therapy in this vulnerable population and the comparative performance of different administration routes remain largely unexplored. Here, we established a cyclophosphamide-induced neutropenic murine sepsis model to evaluate the therapeutic potential of a phage cocktail against CRKP. We demonstrate that both intravenous and intraperitoneal phage administration achieve substantial bacterial load reduction and significant attenuation of systemic inflammation, revealing that phage therapy retains a robust positive response even in the absence of a fully functional host immune system. These findings underscore the clinical translational potential of phage as a viable alternative to antibiotics for combating CRKP infections in immunocompromised patients and provide critical evidence supporting intravenous phage delivery as a feasible administration route.

Microbiology Spectrum.title: Influence of RPMI agar thickness, storage time, and medium source on Candida MIC determination: implications for standardization of gradient diffusion susceptibility testing.
Microbiology Spectrum.abstract: [UNLABELLED] Gradient diffusion susceptibility testing may be influenced by pre-analytical variables. We evaluated the effects of RPMI agar thickness, plate age, and medium source on MIC determination using Candida albicans, Candida parapsilosis, and Candida krusei quality control strains. Increasing agar thickness was consistently associated with higher MICs, whereas plate age and medium source showed less consistent variation. Comparison with Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute (CLSI) broth microdilution showed reproducible reference-method MICs across independent runs in contrast to variation observed with gradient diffusion susceptibility testing across agar conditions. These findings identify agar thickness as an important pre-analytical variable in gradient diffusion MIC determination and support careful standardization of agar depth in diffusion-based antifungal susceptibility testing. [IMPORTANCE] Reliable antifungal susceptibility results are important for detecting reduced susceptibility to antifungal drugs and supporting appropriate treatment decisions. Because these results can be affected by how the test is performed, maintaining standardized testing conditions is essential for obtaining reproducible results across laboratories. In this study, we examined whether the thickness and age of the testing medium, as well as its source, affect gradient strip susceptibility results for Candida quality-control strains. We found that changes in agar thickness were consistently associated with changes in measured MICs, whereas plate age and medium source showed less consistent effects. These findings show that careful control of agar depth is important for improving the consistency and reliability of gradient strip antifungal susceptibility testing.

Microbiology Spectrum.title: Assessing soluble and insoluble calcium sources for growth, biofilm formation, and biomineralization in Bacillus subtilis.
Microbiology Spectrum.abstract: Biofilms formed by soil microbes hold immense potential for bioremediation, carbon dioxide sequestration, and the development of sustainable cementitious materials. However, quantifying the complex temporal coupling among bacterial growth, extracellular matrix (ECM) production, and mineralization dynamics remains challenging because these processes are inherently non-linear and high-throughput assays introduce signal noise. To address this, we utilized an automated kinetic framework to evaluate the biomineralization competence of Bacillus subtilis under varying calcium regimes. Our results demonstrate that calcium carbonate promotes microbial growth as effectively as soluble calcium acetate, indicating that B. subtilis actively solubilizes the crystalline powder. Despite this growth efficacy, calcium carbonate was an inadequate source for macro-calcite production compared to organic salts. By quantifying expression from the sinI promoter, which initiates SinI production to activate matrix synthesis, we suggested that calcium-acetate-driven ECM expression significantly enhances the structural template required for robust biomineralization. Kinetic expression analysis and consolidation assays indicate that overproduced ECM partially mitigates crystalline calcite growth defects, offering a baseline for utilizing mineral-rich construction waste.IMPORTANCEBiomineralization in Bacillus subtilis has been studied as a potential avenue for developing engineered living materials (ELMs). However, organic calcium salts, such as calcium acetate and calcium lactate, typically yield higher bioconversion efficiencies than certain inorganic sources often used in construction. This advantage has been largely attributed to the metabolic utilization of the organic anion as a carbon source, thereby promoting local alkalinity. Here, our experiments indicate that this limitation is influenced by structural and regulatory constraints rather than purely chemical barriers. Moreover, we explored a targeted synthetic biology approach to address this by genetically decoupling matrix production from native environmental sensing, thereby engineering strains with increased matrix production that can partially overcome the limitations of non-inductive substrates. This approach can contribute to sustainable construction technologies, moving toward actively programmed ELMs.

EMBO Reports.title: Stability and tethering of the preconoidal rings in Toxoplasma gondii.
EMBO Reports.abstract: Apicomplexan parasites rely on a specialized apical cytoskeleton to generate the forces required for motility and host-cell invasion. At its core lies the conoid, composed of spiraling tubulin fibers capped by three preconoidal rings (PCRs), which anchor the actin nucleator Formin 1 and contribute to force transmission at the parasite apex. Here, we refine the molecular organization and function of the PCRs in Toxoplasma gondii. We show that PCR composition and stability change during parasite maturation, with a subset of PCR proteins, Pcr2 and Pcr3, adopting a characteristic half-ring organization. We identify MyoL, a divergent pseudomyosin, as a previously unrecognized PCR component. MyoL is essential for efficient gliding and invasion, and its depletion partially detaches the PCRs from the conoid. Structure-function analysis further identifies the MyoL neck and tail as critical for PCR localization and activity. Together, our findings provide new insight into the organization of this conserved apicomplexan complex and reveal an unexpected architectural role for a pseudomyosin in maintaining the PCR-conoid interface.

EMBO Reports.title: Iroquois complex creates an anti-cancerized epithelial field against malignant tumorigenesis.
EMBO Reports.abstract: Some epithelial regions appear intrinsically resistant to malignancy, yet how such anti-cancerized fields are established remains elusive. Here, we show in Drosophila that the Iroquois Complex (Iro-C), a group of transcriptional repressors specifically expressed in the notum region of the wing imaginal epithelium, creates an anti-cancerized field against malignant tumorigenesis. Clones of cells with Ras activation and cell polarity defects (RasV12/scrib-/-) develop into malignant tumors in the pouch and hinge regions of the wing disc yet fail to overgrow in the notum. Mechanistically, intrinsic Iro-C expression in the notum represses upd/IL-6 transcription, thereby preventing JAK-STAT activation essential for driving malignant growth. Forced expression of Upd/IL-6 converts the notum into a tumor-prone field, whereas forced expression of Iro-C in the pouch and hinge abolishes RasV12/scrib-/- tumorigenesis. Our findings provide a mechanistic explanation for how some epithelial regions, such as distal segments of the kidney, where Iro-C/IRX1 is specifically expressed, exhibit resistance to cancer development.

mBio.title: Pathogenesis and natural history of Machupo virus infection in nonhuman primates.
mBio.abstract: [UNLABELLED] The mammarenavirus Machupo virus (MACV) is the causative agent of Bolivian hemorrhagic fever (BHF) and is associated with high mortality rates in humans and nonhuman primates (NHPs). There are currently no approved vaccines or treatments to combat BHF. As there are eight genetically distinct lineages of MACV, medical countermeasures are needed to protect against all strains within these lineages. While rodent models have been developed for a few strains of MACV, NHPs most faithfully reproduce human disease. However, NHP models have only been described for two strains of MACV. Here, we assessed the pathogenic potential of two genetically distinct strains of MACV representing two different lineages in cynomolgus and/or African green monkeys (AGM). Both MACV strains caused severe multisystemic disease consistent with BHF, often resulting in fatality with the lineage III strain resulting in uniform lethality in both NHP species and the lineage VIII strain resulting in uniform lethality in AGM. Pathology was consistent among the MACV strains and NHP species with primary involvement of the gastrointestinal and lymphoid systems with the central nervous system showing variable but widespread dissemination of MACV antigen. Spatial proteomics showed that MACV antigen was most prevalent in neurons (MAP2+) and Purkinje cells (MAP2+/Calbindin+). Multi-omics assessment of circulating mRNA and proteins showed the overall phenotype of BHF was similar between species; however, the magnitude of the inflammatory response diverged at late timepoints. Overall, MACV infection of NHP recapitulated BHF in humans driven by a dysregulated innate response resulting in vascular inflammation and hemodynamic instability. [IMPORTANCE] Machupo virus (MACV) is a deadly and understudied mammarenavirus that causes severe disease known as Bolivian hemorrhagic fever (BHF) with high mortality rates in symptomatic humans. MACV is transmitted to humans by contact with the vesper mouse and has significant outbreak potential. No licensed vaccine or antivirals against MACV exist. Well-characterized animal models are critically needed to test the efficacy of promising candidate medical countermeasures against MACV and to understand how MACV causes disease. Here, we developed several new nonhuman primate models that accurately reproduced human BHF. We utilized spatial proteomics to reveal specific cell types involved in MACV infection, including those within the central nervous system, and employed a multi-omics approach to reveal circulating mRNA and protein biomarkers driving fatal disease outcomes. Our comprehensive investigation of the response to MACV infection in a highly translational species can be exploited to develop new countermeasures to combat BHF.

mBio.title: Human monoclonal antibody targeting the O-antigen protects against multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae complex.
mBio.abstract: Klebsiella pneumoniae (Kp) are encapsulated gram-negative bacteria that cause healthcare-associated and severe community-acquired infections. The global emergence of carbapenem-resistant strains has led the World Health Organization to designate K. pneumoniae a "critical priority" pathogen. This study aimed to identify human monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) with therapeutic potential against multidrug-resistant K. pneumoniae. Using a target-agnostic strategy, we selected human mAbs elicited during an asymptomatic infection with K. pneumoniae. We evaluated the antibody binding to bacterial surface antigens by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), analytical flow cytometry, and immunoblotting. In vitro, the mAbs were tested by complement-mediated killing and macrophage uptake assays using Kp clinical isolates of differing serotypes. Finally, we evaluated the therapeutic efficacy of the mAbs in a murine pneumonia model with carbapenem-resistant K. pneumoniae. Among the four IgG antibodies identified, mAbKPNA-14 demonstrated specific binding to K. pneumoniae wzi50:O3b and cross-reactivity with O-antigen type O3/O3a. mAbKPNA-14 significantly enhanced complement-mediated killing (p < 0.01) and macrophage phagocytosis. In vivo, the therapeutic administration of mAbKPNA-14 reduced bacterial load in the lungs by over 100-fold compared to the control groups (p < 0.001) and prevented systemic dissemination. This study describes a human mAb that binds to O3b and O3/O3a O-antigens and confers in vivo protection against drug-resistant K. pneumoniae. These findings support the therapeutic potential of mAbs and describe a strategy for isolating and identifying protective mAbs targeting multidrug-resistant bacteria.IMPORTANCEMultidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae is a critical global health threat for which new therapeutic approaches are urgently needed. Here, we identify a naturally elicited human monoclonal antibody, mAbKPNA-14, which recognizes the O3b O-antigen and cross-reacts with related O3/O3a O-antigens. The antibody promotes complement-mediated killing and macrophage uptake and, when administered therapeutically, reduces pulmonary bacterial burden by more than 100-fold and prevents systemic dissemination in a mouse model of carbapenem-resistant K. pneumoniae pneumonia. These findings demonstrate that protective human antibodies can be isolated directly from individuals following K. pneumoniae infection and identify O-antigen as a promising target for antibody-based therapy. More broadly, our target-agnostic approach provides a strategy for discovering naturally occurring protective antibodies against multidrug-resistant bacterial pathogens.

Science Bulletin.title: Non-Bloch exceptional points detached from branch points.
Science Bulletin.abstract: Exceptional points (EPs) in non-Hermitian Bloch band structures are branch points of the energy Riemann surface, connected pairwise by non-Hermitian Fermi arcs whose topology determines eigenvalue knots. Under open boundary conditions (OBCs), non-Hermitian skin effects enforce complex momenta and yield non-Bloch band structures, where EPs absent from the periodic spectrum-termed non-Bloch EPs-can emerge. Here, we show theoretically and experimentally that non-Bloch EPs are detached from branch points and instead emerge at saddle points of generalized-Brillouin-zone (GBZ) geometry within a single Riemann sheet. By identifying each band's sub-GBZ as a band-dependent base manifold, the parameter space over which its energy is defined, we establish general criteria for the emergence of such non-Bloch EPs in multiband systems. Using a reciprocal non-Hermitian Lieb lattice with geometry-dependent skin effects, we demonstrate that a change from rectangular to parallelogram geometry induces such non-Bloch EPs at energies distinct from any Bloch EP. In non-Bloch band structures, branch points carrying OBC eigenenergies do not produce EPs but instead appear as Whitney cusps-geometric singularities that anchor non-Bloch Fermi arcs and continue to govern eigenvalue knots. Measurements of these knots confirm the detachment of non-Bloch EPs from branch points, in sharp contrast to Bloch systems where the two are unified. Our results decouple non-Bloch EPs from the braiding topology associated with Fermi arcs and reveal the fundamental role of band-dependent base manifolds in reshaping non-Hermitian band structures.

Nature Ecology & Evolution.title: Meta-analysis shows that immunization reduces amphibian susceptibility to the chytrid fungus

Biogeosciences.title: Building a random forest machine learning model for annual Net Ecosystem Exchange estimation in agricultural fields using discontinuous atmospheric Eddy Covariance measurements
Biogeosciences.abstract: Building a random forest machine learning model for annual Net Ecosystem Exchange estimation in agricultural fields using discontinuous atmospheric Eddy Covariance measurements Camille Pery, Pierre Polsenaere, Eric Lamaud, Natacha Volto, Nathalie Long, Jonathan Deborde, Shunko Bolsée, Olivier Philippine, Vona Méléder, and Christine Dupuy Biogeosciences, 23, 8477–8505, https://doi.org/10.5194/bg-23-8477-2026, 2026 This study evaluates the potential of combining continuous atmospheric CO2 flux measurements with IA modelling to estimate carbon budgets in agricultural crops in a French wetland. Modelling strategies were developed to capture their phenological and management-related carbon dynamics. Our results provide a pragmatic framework to derive plot-scale carbon budgets and offers promising perspectives for improving regional carbon flux inventories and assessing climate-smart agricultural practices.

Biogeosciences.title: Evaluating GNSS-T VOD sensitivity to plant water dynamics, rainfall interception, and dew in a coniferous forest
Biogeosciences.abstract: Evaluating GNSS-T VOD sensitivity to plant water dynamics, rainfall interception, and dew in a coniferous forest Konstantin Schellenberg, Sinikka J. Paulus, Ronald Queck, David Chaparro, Oliver Binks, Maurizio Mencuccini, Sharath S. Paligi, Henrik Hartmann, Christiane Schmullius, Clémence Dubois, and Thomas Jagdhuber Biogeosciences, 23, 8507–8536, https://doi.org/10.5194/bg-23-8507-2026, 2026 We evaluated Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) signals to monitor forest water storage, helping to close an important observational gap in plant hydraulics and micrometeorology at stand-scale. We show that signal losses in the canopy are strongly linked to three-dimensionally modeled rainfall interception. However, detecting subtle fluxes, such as internal water dynamics, dew and intercepted light rain is inhibited by signal noise, and the hydraulics properties of the ecosystem.

Biogeosciences.title: Climate warming-induced agricultural nitrous oxide emissions can offset mitigation benefits of fertiliser reduction
Biogeosciences.abstract: Climate warming-induced agricultural nitrous oxide emissions can offset mitigation benefits of fertiliser reduction Jize Jiang, Lenny H. E. Winkel, Andrea Stenke, Magdalena Necpalova, Moritz Laub, Iris Feigenwinter, Nina Buchmann, and Johan Six Biogeosciences, 23, 8537–8557, https://doi.org/10.5194/bg-23-8537-2026, 2026 We studied how fertiliser management and a warming climate affect nitrous oxide emissions from agricultural soils in Switzerland over the past fourty years. Using computer simulations and nationwide data, we found that lower fertiliser use reduced emissions, but rising temperatures cancelled part of these mitigations. The results show a trade-off between mitigation actions and environmental-driven feedback, highlighting future efforts must also account for the effects of a changing climate.

Molecular Biology and Evolution.title: Whole-blood transcriptomics reveal molecular compatibility and complementarity across advanced therapies in ulcerative colitis
Molecular Biology and Evolution.abstract: AbstractBackground and AimsDespite an expanding therapeutic landscape, an efficacy ceiling persists with advanced monotherapies in ulcerative colitis (UC). We used longitudinal whole-blood transcriptomics to characterize molecular compatibility, therapy-specific effects with potential complementarity, and potential cross-therapy resistance correction.MethodsAdults with endoscopically active UC (Mayo endoscopic sub-score [MES] ≥2) initiating anti-tumor necrosis factor (anti-TNF), vedolizumab (VDZ), tofacitinib (TFC), or ustekinumab (UST) underwent whole-blood RNA sequencing at baseline and/or post-induction endoscopy. Endoscopic improvement was defined as MES ≤1. Response- and resistance-associated signatures were compared across differentially expressed genes (DEGs), enriched biological processes, and transcription factor (TF) activities. Potential correction required an opposite-direction response effect ≥50% of the corresponding resistance effect.ResultsAmong 314 treatment cycles from 234 patients (514 RNA samples), 47.6% achieved endoscopic improvement. Anti-TNF, VDZ, and TFC response-associated signatures were broadly concordant across molecular layers while retaining therapy-specific features. UST showed no significant response-associated DEGs but retained distinct pathway- and TF-level signals. In parallel, cross-therapy response-associated effects opposed resistance-associated features, with correlations of −0.89 to −1.00 for genes, −0.64 to −0.84 for biological processes, and −0.52 to −0.76 for TF activities. Against anti-TNF resistance, VDZ met the potential-correction criterion for 70% of DEGs, 79% of biological processes, and 96% of TF activities, including all 20 resistance processes with the largest absolute enrichment scores.ConclusionsWhole-blood transcriptomics identified compatible shared responses, therapy-specific molecular effects, and potential cross-therapy compensation. These findings generate hypotheses for biologically informed combination strategies requiring prospective validation, rather than evidence of efficacy or synergy.

Molecular Biology and Evolution.title: Time-to-response in acute severe ulcerative colitis: when to continue, optimize, or stop treatment
Molecular Biology and Evolution.abstract: AbstractAcute severe ulcerative colitis is an emergency in which treatment selection and timing are inseparable. This narrative review synthesizes published response trajectories and proposes treatment-specific futility windows for inpatient therapies, including intravenous corticosteroids, cyclosporine, infliximab, Janus kinase inhibitors, calcineurin-inhibitor bridging strategies, and sequential rescue. We propose that trajectory should override any protocol day. Deterioration, systemic toxicity, worsening abdominal findings, organ dysfunction, or radiologic complications should prompt immediate escalation and surgical reassessment rather than waiting for a scheduled checkpoint. Conversely, objective improvement without remission may justify cautious continuation. Therapeutic stagnation requires integrating stool frequency, bleeding, systemic features, C-reactive protein, albumin, hemoglobin, imaging, informative endoscopy, pharmacokinetic exposure when available, and surgical risk. For intravenous corticosteroids, assessment starts at admission; day 3 guides rescue preparation; if no deterioration occurs beforehand, lack of meaningful objective improvement by day 5 should prompt rescue therapy or surgery. Cyclosporine usually declares its trajectory within the first week. For infliximab, days 5-7 are the principal clinical decision window; stable patients with inadequate exposure may undergo optimization, with later reassessment reserved for partial responders. Tofacitinib and upadacitinib may act rapidly; off-label rescue evidence remains observational, and absent improvement by days 5-7 is concerning. When a calcineurin inhibitor (CNI) bridges to a maintenance biologic, acute decisions should be based on response to the CNI, not the maintenance agent. Sequential third-line rescue should be exceptional, multidisciplinary, time-limited, and never delay colectomy when deterioration or a surgical indication is present. Across therapies, reassessment must be paired with continuous surgical involvement.

Nucleic Acids Research.title: SynCED: the Synthetic Chemical Exposome Database.
Nucleic Acids Research.abstract: The Synthetic Chemical Exposome Database (SynCED) (https://syncedb.ca) is a substantially updated and expanded version of the Toxin and Toxin Target Database (T3DB). SynCED provides rich data on 316 418 synthetic chemicals from diverse chemical, toxicological, exposure, and regulatory sources. The synthetic chemical exposome comprises a vast and rapidly expanding range of anthropogenic chemicals, yet information on their sources, uses, biological effects, toxicity, and molecular interactions remains fragmented across numerous resources. SynCED addresses this problem by consolidating this information and linking most known synthetic chemicals with standardized chemical names and identifiers, compound descriptions, predicted or measured physicochemical properties, reference spectral data, exposure and use information, toxicological data, and biological targets or interactions. Literature-derived compound descriptions and functional annotations were built using the Chemical Functional Ontology (ChemFOnt) Fact Finder pipeline, which extracts semantically defined chemical-relation-entity associations while retaining supporting evidence and provenance. In addition to literature-derived biological target information, SynCED also incorporates ligand-based protein-target predictions to extend the coverage of chemicals lacking experimentally characterized interactions. To facilitate compound identification using non-target or suspect screening, SynCED provides extensive search utilities supporting searches by chemical structure, toxicity, text, mass, molecular weight, elemental composition, ESI-MS, EI-MS, and NMR spectra (both measured and predicted) as well as searches by target sequence (protein and DNA). It also supports database browsing by chemical names, ClassyFire chemical taxonomy and exposure source. Together, these features extend T3DB to turn SynCED into a broader, more provenance-aware database, that supports suspect or non-target screening, chemical exposure and hazard assessment, mechanistic studies, and general chemical exposomics research.

Nucleic Acids Research.title: FusionGDB 3.0: integrating breakpoints, generating personalized sequences, and inferring tumorigenic scenarios for human fusion genes.
Nucleic Acids Research.abstract: FusionGDB has served diverse biological, health, and clinical research communities as a unique functional annotation knowledgebase of human fusion genes. In this study, we report an updated resource of human fusion gene annotation (FusionGDB 3.0), available at https://compbio.uth.edu/FusionGDB/. FusionGDB 3.0 includes substantial content updates: 156K up-to-date human fusion genes established by integrating 216K RNA-seq-based and 100K WGS-based breakpoint events, comprehensive open reading frame annotations, protein domain retention searches, and 1.13 million personalized fusion protein sequences reflecting individual nsSNVs from TCGA and CCLE, as well as N- and C-truncated protein sequences alongside canonical in-frame products. Furthermore, it incorporates 18K potential tumorigenic scenarios, supported by evidence from the literature, spanning drug-targetable gene group fusions, the epigenomic architecture around breakpoint junctions, and therapeutic prioritization scoring. FusionGDB 3.0 establishes a systematic framework for the functional annotation of coding structural variants. FusionGDB 3.0 serves as a pivotal reference knowledgebase for the genomics, oncology, and precision pharmacology communities, while also functioning as a foundational benchmark dataset for training and validating machine learning models, structural biology platforms, and AI-driven therapeutic discovery pipelines.

Nucleic Acids Research.title: CIViC 2026: expanding cancer variant curation with AI, genome-wide biomarkers, and genomic regions.
Nucleic Acids Research.abstract: The CIViC (Clinical Interpretations of Variants in Cancer) knowledgebase (https://civicdb.org) remains one of the few free, unrestricted knowledgebases for the distribution of somatic cancer variant interpretations. CIViC leverages public curation and expert moderation to address the bottleneck problem of cancer variant interpretation for patient care. As the curation platform for ClinGen Somatic Cancer, the CIViC knowledge model is informed by multiple experts across disparate fields in cancer and, in turn, acts as a model for cancer variant classification and representation. In order to capture a wider range of genomic variations, several updates to CIViC's data and curation model have been made with a focus on maintaining familiar workflows and user interface layouts. A new top-level entity called the Feature represents Genes, Fusions, Regions for large-scale structural variations, and Factors for genome-wide biomarkers. Accompanying Variants capture information unique to each genomic event. Molecular Profiles enable the curation of complex combinations of these Variants. CIViC has also developed a system for approval and submission of Assertions to ClinVar, guidance for the use of AI in curation and moderation of content, and additional capabilities such as source retraction monitoring and an advanced query builder.

Nucleic Acids Research.title: CovPDB 2.0: an expanded covalent protein-ligand interactome.
Nucleic Acids Research.abstract: The rational design of covalently binding inhibitors to specifically block selected target proteins has become a common strategy in drug discovery. Such design is based on structural insights into how electrophilic ligands bind to nucleophilic residues. CovPDB v1.0 provided high-resolution cocrystal structures of biologically relevant covalent protein-ligand complexes curated from the Protein Data Bank. Here, we describe CovPDB v2.0, a substantially extended release that addresses three main limitations of the original resource. First, to reflect the numerous novel covalently binding ligands developed and structurally elucidated over the past 4 years, we have classified, annotated, and integrated these entries into the database. This expands the collection from ~2300 to ~6200 protein-ligand complexes, comprising ~3600 pre-reactive ligands, ~1300 target proteins, 119 warheads, and 27 reaction types. Second, we expanded the structural scope beyond experimental cocrystals by generating AlphaFold3 cofolding models for additional ~6800 covalent complexes for which we had experimental evidence for a covalent ligand binding. Third, we added ~7100 non-covalent complexes in which the binding-site cysteines are annotated with a predicted reactivity and ligandability scores. A redesigned web interface allows users to browse, filter, and cross-search experimental, modelled, and ligandable-cysteine entries. CovPDB 2.0 is freely accessible at https://www.pharmbioinf.uni-freiburg.de/covpdb.

Nucleic Acids Research.title: canSAR 2026-an update to the public drug discovery knowledgebase.
Nucleic Acids Research.abstract: canSAR (https://cansar.ai) serves as the world's largest public platform for cancer drug discovery and translational research. It serves as an exploration and hypothesis generation platform for drug discovery through (i) fully integrating large, multidisciplinary data from public resources, as well as bespoke curated data, creating a connected, navigable drug discovery knowledge map; and (ii) applying a suite of machine learning and AI tools to generate novel insights. We share the latest updates to canSAR highlighting growth across all data, enhancements to the predictive algorithms, and continued improvements to the user experience. We leverage our latest open science chemical handling and druggability prediction tools to provide traceable insights. An increased focus of the platform is to provide "in-line" support and guidance to drug discovery exploration. We report the first incarnation of our high-fidelity, agentic-AI-generated, context-specific summaries, which we provide across the website for all human proteins to further aid users in synthesis and distillation of key information.

Nucleic Acids Research.title: Europe PMC in 2026.
Nucleic Acids Research.abstract: Europe PMC (https://europepmc.org/) is an open access database of life-science literature that delivers open science to a wide audience through an open web interface, APIs, and bulk downloads. It brings together 48 million abstracts, 12 million full text published articles, and supplementary files and 1.2 million preprints, 76 000 of them full text, and makes them findable through dozens of search axes. Europe PMC is supported by 35 European and international funders to deliver a global open infrastructure and support their open access policies and metrics analysis. Europe PMC enriches the literature with 2 billion text-mined annotations, and links to dozens of biological databases. New developments to the Europe PMC platform since the last database update in 2023 include: (i) harnessing AI to enhance discovery through new machine learning generated annotations and working towards Europe PMC as a knowledge layer for LLMs; (ii) enhancing product development UX/UI capabilities, showcased through a new advanced search; (iii) improving literature discovery by text mining supplementary files; (iv) improving persistent identifier coverage and expanding the citation network.

Nucleic Acids Research.title: DriverDBv5: a multi-omics integration database for cancer driver gene research.
Nucleic Acids Research.abstract: Cancer is driven by alterations across multiple molecular layers, but whether multi-omics drivers carry prognostic weight has received little systematic attention. DriverDBv5 (https://driverdb.bioinfomics.org/) extends DriverDB from driver identification to prognostic evaluation. It has been expanded to 187 cohorts, 43 862 patients, and 129 655 samples, with 154 cohorts from non-TCGA (The Cancer Genome Atlas) repositories reconciled by a generalized multi-omics barcode. Driver genes can be evaluated with Cox and mixture cure models, with machine learning on the full multi-omics feature matrix, and for the joint prognostic effect of alterations in two omics layers. The Customized Analysis module has grown from 4 to 10 tools for user-defined gene sets, subgroups, and covariates, and a human body map offers an anatomical entry point. DriverDBv5 thus reveals not only which alterations drive a tumor, but also which of them relate to patient outcome.

Nucleic Acids Research.title: ADCdb 2.0: clinical landscape and ADMET profiles of antibody-drug conjugates.
Nucleic Acids Research.abstract: Systematically characterizing antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) is essential for understanding their therapeutic properties, guiding molecular design, and supporting clinical development. Recently, the expanding clinical landscape of ADCs has generated extensive information on target antigens, therapeutic indications, and clinical trial pipelines, providing a valuable foundation for informing ADC development strategies. Moreover, ADMET profiles are critical for understanding the in vivo disposition, efficacy, and safety of ADCs. Integrating these accumulating clinical and pharmacological data is therefore necessary to enrich the evidence available for ADC development. In this study, ADCdb was updated to provide (i) detailed clinical landscape information for 542 ADCs, together with >3000 manually curated clinical trials from registries across nine registries and clinical trial platforms; (ii) >4000 ADMET profiles, including quantitative pharmacokinetic parameters and descriptive annotations supported by relevant references; and (iii) expanded pharmacological information and biological activity data comprising 13 088 ADC entries and 24 821 activity records, as well as ADC-specific functional annotations for 389 ADCs. Interactive visualization tools and antigen- and disease-centered search modules further enable systematic exploration of ADC composition, therapeutic indications, and clinical development. ADCdb 2.0 is expected to serve as a valuable resource for rational optimization of ADCs, and is accessible at https://idrblab.org/adcdb/.

Nucleic Acids Research.title: LACA: a cross-species single-cell resource for exploring longevity and aging-associated cellular and molecular programs.
Nucleic Acids Research.abstract: Different species can have various maximum lifespans, some with exceptional longevity, yet the underlying cellular and molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. Despite rapid advances in single-cell transcriptomics, resources that systematically connect single-cell gene expression profiles to species lifespan are limited. We hereby present the Longevity & Aging Cell Atlas (LACA), a database that integrates single-cell transcriptomic datasets across 134 species with their maximum lifespans. LACA includes over 148 million cells with 190 annotated cell types from single-cell datasets. LACA also has a cross-species analytical toolbox of longevity gene comparison, gene-lifespan correlation, and cell-lifespan correlation. These tools allow researchers to better interpret both evolutionarily conserved longevity mechanisms and the evolution of species-specific adaptations in longevity mechanisms without extensive computational expertise. LACA also provides a centenarian single-cell atlas and a human immune aging multi-omics atlas, demonstrating the analytical capability of the resource, as well as 11 different modules for longevity-related analysis, an integrated knowledge graph including curated longevity knowledge bases, and a retrieval-augmented research agent to further facilitate functional interpretation. The database is freely available at https://www.longevityaging.net/ or http://8.142.154.29/LACA/.

The Innovation.title: A unified thermodynamic paradigm for predicting dam-induced thermal hysteresis and ecological reorganization in global rivers
The Innovation.abstract: The global proliferation of dams has created profound yet unpredictable ecological shifts through altered thermal regimes. Here, we develop a unifying paradigm linking dam-induced thermal changes to ecological responses across six continents by introducing two governing parameters (reservoir disturbance coefficient k and latitudinal compensation rate λ). These define a unified function that explains ∼90% of cross-basin variance in thermal hysteresis, triggering synchronized delays of 19.8 ± 13.0 days in ecosystem processes from primary production to organismal life cycles.

FEMS Microbiology Reviews.title: A unit-based framework for understanding fungal copy-number variation: formation, function, evolution, and detection.
FEMS Microbiology Reviews.abstract: Copy-number variation (CNV) is a widespread form of genomic variation across diverse organisms, yet differences in how copy-number changes are defined and described hinder comparisons across studies. Drawing on studies of fungi spanning diverse genome architectures, ploidy states, and reproductive modes, we propose a unit-based operational framework that classifies CNVs at six hierarchical levels according to the genomic unit whose copy number changes. The framework distinguishes this structural unit from the functional unit that most directly accounts for a defined biological effect, while treating the direction and magnitude of copy-number change, architecture, and physical form as complementary descriptors. We use this framework to examine how fungal CNVs arise and are remodelled, and how copy-number changes at different genomic scales give rise to distinct functional consequences. We then consider how selection, structural persistence and reversibility, interactions with other genomic variation, and population processes shape CNV evolution. Finally, we assess how complementary detection approaches resolve copy-number states, unit boundaries, and structural configurations, and how their limitations constrain interpretation. By linking unit-based classification to CNV formation, evidence-based functional attribution, evolutionary trajectories, and detection, this framework supports comparisons across fungal systems and informs a broader understanding of genome plasticity and adaptation.

npj Biofilms & Microbiomes.title: Phages rewire bacterial fitness: beyond killing in host-associated disease
npj Biofilms & Microbiomes.abstract: npj Biofilms and Microbiomes, Published online: 20 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41522-026-01201-6Temperate and lytic phages can redirect host-associated bacterial phenotypes through distinct mechanisms. Lytic phages may attenuate virulence when resistance carries pleiotropic costs, whereas prophage-encoded regulation can directly enhance bacterial fitness. We propose that these outcomes represent complementary routes of phage-mediated phenotypic filtering, determined by how phage susceptibility, resistance pathways, or phage-encoded functions intersect with bacterial traits governing colonization, immunity, and disease.
